days.topic: Topic 17: Proteins and Optical Isomerism · Classifying Amino Acids by Side Chain
days.title: Proteins and amino acids

groups.w: Each has a non-amino-acid part: heme, a lipid, a carbohydrate, a nucleic acid.
The four side-chain interactions; London dispersion is the hydrophobic one, and the disulfide bond is the strongest.
Hydrocarbon side chains. Methionine has S, but S and C share electronegativity 2.5, so C–S–C is nonpolar.
Serine and threonine have –OH, cysteine has –SH and asparagine has an amide: polar but neutral.
EC 3 hydrolases, 4 lyases, 5 isomerases, 6 ligases; oxidoreductases and transferases are classes 1 and 2.
Absolute: one substrate. Group: similar functional groups. Linkage: one type of bond. Stereospecificity: one stereoisomer.
Aspirin blocks prostaglandin synthesis, methotrexate DNA synthesis in cancer cells, sulfa drugs bacterial folic acid; nerve gases are poisons.

groups.n: Need a metal ion as cofactor
groups.w: Catalase Fe, arginase Mn²⁺, hexokinase Mg²⁺, cytochrome oxidase Cu²⁺. Their names look like classes, but these are single enzymes.

days.topic: Topic 19: Lipids · Types by Structure and Membrane Lipids
days.title: Lipids

groups.w: Glycerol + two fatty acids + phosphate + an amino alcohol such as choline.
Linoleic (18:2) becomes arachidonic acid: omega-6. Linolenic (18:3) becomes EPA: omega-3.
They carry an extra grouping: phosphate, a sugar, a nitrogenous base or a protein.
Usually no fatty acids: steroids (cholesterol, sex hormones), prostaglandins and terpenes such as limonene.

days.topic: Lesson 8: GI Drugs · H2 Blockers and PPIs
days.title: GI drugs

groups.w: CRFN: they keep histamine off the H2 receptor of the parietal cell.
Bicarbonate and carbonate make CO₂ (belching); magnesium and aluminum hydroxide make only water.
Given with a PPI: clarithromycin triple, bismuth quadruple and nonbismuth quadruple therapy.
They irritate the GI lining: the anthraquinones aloe, senna and cascara, and bisacodyl (Dulcolax).

days.title: Methods of therapy

groups.w: Drugs (lithium, antipsychotics), electroconvulsive therapy and psychosurgery act on the body.
Freud's tools for insight into unconscious conflicts.
Learning principles change the behavior directly.
The thinking errors that cognitive therapy teaches clients to catch.
